pr_title: kernel: Define application entry point prototype
pr_body:
kernel: Define application entry point prototype
    
Define in a public header the prototype of the (optional) application `main()`.
    
Until now, this was hidden inside the init code, which lead to some tests and samples defining it with the wrong signature.
    
Also this fixes issues when defining this function in C++ code.

~Note that this PR includes #21100, as that fix is necessary for it~
~But I would not merge this PR until after freeze (as it may break apps which have the same issue as fixed in #21100)~

~Fixes #21094~(already fixed)
pr_comments: We should also update https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/reference/kernel/threads/system_threads.html?highlight=main%20function to indicate what happens when ``main()`` returns.

#21094 was fixed by #21363, so as such there is no special need to merge this one. Given that there is some controversy on this one I close it, but leave the branch in case somebody wants to take it further.

issue_context.title: native_posix doesn't call main function that's defined in C++
issue_context.body:
native_posix uses [the following macro:](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/arch/posix/include/posix_cheats.h#L43) 
`#define main(...) zephyr_app_main(__VA_ARGS__)` to rename the app's main to something else (which is presumably linked with a no-op weak symbol that gets overridden by the app's main if it exists).

This works fine in C, but if you define your main function in a C++ file, because the function name isn't the magically special-cased 'main' anymore, the function name gets mangled into something along the lines of `_Z15zephyr_app_mainv` (for `void main(void)`), which results in the main function getting silently ignored.

I'm not sure there's actually any way to make the macro work: you can't use `asm` to specify the name of the symbol in the definition of a function, only the declaration. If it's possible to require main to be `void(void)`, ~the macro could be replaced by a forward declaration of `void main(void) asm("zephyr_app_main")`~ an `extern "C"` forward declaration of zephyr_app_main could be added `#if defined(__cplusplus)`, but this might break existing code. Grepping around, it looks like there's one sample that might be broken by this: https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/master/samples/userspace/prod_consumer/src/main.c#L50.

review_comments: Do we define what happens If the main function does return, e.g., the system will shutdown/power off?
There's no special semantics currently, it will just cause the main thread to exit.

@dbkinder Would you like me to either link to that [part of the documentation](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/reference/kernel/threads/system_threads.html) or replicate in this comment part of it? (It's a bit unclear to me how you would like to proceed)

@andrewboie @aescolar @nashif  I guess I was looking for a defined behavior of the system if the main function returns and that thread is terminated. Architecturally, what code does the processor execute after that then and what will the system be doing?  If that's not defined by Zephyr, then so be it.

another ready thread will then run, which may be the idle thread if no other threads are present or ready to run.

main is just another thread. nothing special happens when it returns.
if all threads exit then the system just sits there in the idle thread for each cpu, there's always at least an idle thread to run.
Ah.  Thanks for clarifying that for me @andrewboie, maybe it's obvious that there's always an idle thread around for a CPU to run.
Why don't you name it `ztest_unit.h` or `ztest_unit_main.h` ? It seems more coherent.

Actually I'm not getting the purpose of this commit, even for unit test one still need to include `ztest.h` because there may be some required definitions there, right ? Even if not, you are still building `ztest.c` for unit tests and `ztest.h` is still including this header  ....

It seems to me that this is just bringing more complication ... but I may be wrong here.

The purpose of this, is being able to compile ztest_unit_main.c without pulling all other zephyr headers into that translation unit. 
This ztest_unit_main defines the Linux executable `main()`. Meaning, it is just part of the "unit tests framework".
Compiling it with other zephyr headers as it was, complicates things quite a lot unnecessarily. Separating it, is the easiest way of having the new definition this PR introduces not create problems in the unit test framework. It should also avoid other intermingling problems in the future.
Wrt. this new header in particular, it is just what this `main()` requires from the rest of the unit test framework.
